learn.title: How Electric Vehicles Work
learn.intro: Electric vehicles are transforming transportation by replacing gasoline engines with clean electric motors. Understanding how EVs work—from their powerful motors to regenerative braking and convenient home charging—is key to embracing sustainable mobility and reducing carbon emissions on our roads.
learn.c1_text: An electric motor converts electrical energy into motion using magnetic fields, delivering instant torque. Unlike gasoline engines, EVs have far fewer moving parts—about 20 compared to over 200 in internal combustion engines—making them simpler, quieter, and more efficient.
learn.c2_text: Regenerative braking captures energy normally lost during braking, converting it back into electricity to recharge the battery. When you ease off the pedal, the motor acts as a generator, slowing the car while storing energy for later use.
learn.c3_text: Charging an EV is as simple as plugging into a wall outlet or using a dedicated charging station. Level 1 uses 120V outlets; Level 2 uses 240V for faster charging. India aims to electrify 30% of new vehicle sales by 2030 under FAME-II.
learn.stat2: EVs convert 89% of energy to motion vs 30% for gas cars

learn.title: Small Wind Turbines for Homes
learn.intro: Small wind turbines offer a decentralized way to generate clean electricity right where it's needed—on rooftops or rural properties. They complement solar power and empower communities to reduce reliance on fossil fuels while building local energy resilience.
learn.c1_text: Small wind turbines capture kinetic energy from moving air using rotor blades that spin when wind flows over them. The spinning shaft turns a generator, producing electricity. Unlike large turbines, these systems typically range from 100 watts to 100 kW.
learn.c2_text: These systems connect directly to home electrical panels, often paired with batteries for storage. Tower height matters—ideally 30 feet above nearby obstacles—to access stronger, steadier winds. A typical residential turbine can offset 500–1,500 kWh annually.
learn.c3_text: India ranks 4th globally in wind capacity with 40 GW installed by 2023. Small turbines are gaining traction in states like Tamil Nadu and Gujarat. MNRE supports small wind projects under its hybrid policy framework to boost rural electrification.
learn.stat4: Cut-in speed: as low as 6 mph (2.7 m/s)

learn.title: Iron-Air Batteries for Storage
learn.intro: Iron-air batteries represent a breakthrough in long-duration energy storage, capable of storing power for over 100 hours. These low-cost, scalable systems could revolutionize how we store renewable energy when the sun isn’t shining or wind isn’t blowing.
learn.c1_text: Iron-air batteries use rust (iron oxide) as the cathode material and operate by reversibly forming and breaking chemical bonds between iron and oxygen. During discharge, iron oxidizes; during charging, it reduces back—storing energy chemically for weeks or months.
learn.c2_text: Unlike lithium-ion batteries that last hours, iron-air systems can store energy for days or even weeks. They’re ideal for seasonal storage or backup during extended outages. Their modular design allows scaling from homes to grid-level installations.
learn.c3_text: India plans to add 500 GWh of battery storage by 2030. While iron-air tech isn’t yet commercialized here, pilot projects are underway. The government’s National Mission on Strategic Systems emphasizes R&D for indigenous long-duration storage solutions.
learn.stat4: Iron-air systems can store energy for 100+ hours

learn.title: Solar PV and the Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar photovoltaic (PV) panels convert sunlight directly into electricity through the photoelectric effect—a phenomenon that earned Einstein his Nobel Prize. As solar becomes the world’s cheapest electricity source, understanding how PV works helps unlock its full potential.
learn.c1_text: A typical rooftop system includes panels, mounting structures, inverters, and meters. Panels produce DC power during daylight, which flows to an inverter that changes it to AC power used by lights, fans, and other devices in your home.
learn.c3_text: India has become a global solar leader with over 75 GW of installed capacity by 2024. The International Solar Alliance, launched by India, aims to mobilize $1 trillion in solar investments globally. Rooftop solar remains underutilized despite strong policy push.

learn.title: Microgrids for Energy Independence
learn.intro: Microgrids are localized energy networks that can operate independently from the main grid. They enhance energy security, support remote communities, and improve disaster resilience—making them essential tools in the shift toward decentralized, clean energy systems.
learn.c1_text: When the main grid fails, smart switches isolate the microgrid in a process called 'islanding.' Advanced controllers manage supply and demand in real time, balancing generation with load to maintain stable voltage and frequency within the local network.
learn.c3_text: India has over 10,000 microgrids serving remote villages through initiatives like the Smart Grid Mission. Startups like Tata Power and Husk Power are deploying solar microgrids in states like Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, improving lives while cutting diesel dependence.
learn.stat2: Microgrids reduce diesel use by up to 70%
learn.stat4: Over 130 million people lack electricity access globally

learn.title: Rooftop Solar in India
learn.intro: Rooftop solar empowers Indian households and businesses to generate their own clean electricity, reducing bills and easing pressure on the national grid. Supported by policies like net metering, it plays a vital role in achieving India’s ambitious renewable energy targets.
learn.c1_text: Net metering allows consumers to get billed only for the difference between what they generate and consume. If you export surplus power to the grid, your meter spins backward, giving you credit at the same rate you pay for electricity—effectively turning your roof into a power plant.
learn.c3_text: India aims for 450 GW of renewable capacity by 2030, including 280 GW from solar. The government launched a Rs 24,000 crore rooftop solar subsidy scheme in 2024 to accelerate adoption among residential users. Several states offer additional incentives.
learn.stat2: Only 12 GW rooftop solar installed so far
learn.stat3: Subsidy covers 40% of system cost for homes
learn.stat4: Average household saves ₹30,000/year with net metering
